text.p: Scotland on Wednesday rejected the proposal of playing their controversial rematch with Estonia in Cyprus in February.
Now they are likely to be offered the former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan as an alternative by the Estonian football authorities.
Scotland say their followers, the "tartan army", should not have to fly for 5-1/2 hours to Cyprus, though Azerbaijan could involve a flight of eight or nine hours.
Estonian Football Association secretary Ainar Leppanen confirmed on Wednesday that they offered Cyprus as the venue for the rematch on Tuesday, February 11.
But the Scottish Football Association will reject that offer because they say it is too far for cash-strapped fans.

It looks increasingly likely that FIFA, who ordered the replay after the infamous October 9 match-which was halted after three seconds because of a change in the start time, will have to step into the dispute and order a venue.

"I have received confirmation from the Cypriot football authorities that they could stage the match on February 11," said Leppanen. "That would either be in Limassol or Paralimni with the kick-off to be agreed nearer the time.
"I have heard that Scotland are not happy with the suggestion of Cyprus. I am sorry it is such a long flight but it is a long way for our supporters as well.

"We cannot have the match in Tallinn because of the severe weather conditions in Estonia at that time. In any case, it would cost Scottish fans more to live in somewhere like France or Italy than it would Cyprus."
Estonia's national team will be in Cyprus from December until April for training but Scotland are ready to resist any move to go there.
SFA spokesman David Findlay confirmed reception of a fax from the Estonians saying they would like the match to be in Cyprus in February.
"We will reject that suggestion as we do not see why Scotland supporters should have to make a flight of more than five hours to go to see this match.
"It is up to Estonia to come up with another venue or for FIFA to get themselves involved in this."
Scotland suggest the game should go to southern France, Italy, Spain or Portugal.
